s.en: build and execute command lines from standard input
s.es: construye y ejecuta comandos a partir de la entrada estándar

tip.es: Por defecto xargs separa por espacios: con nombres que contengan espacios usa «find … -print0 | xargs -0 …».
tip.en: By default xargs splits on whitespace: with names containing spaces use "find … -print0 | xargs -0 …".

o.es: Los elementos de la entrada vienen separados por un byte nulo (par de «find -print0»); seguro con espacios.
o.en: Input items are separated by a null byte (pairs with "find -print0"); safe with spaces.

o.es: Pasa como máximo N argumentos por ejecución.
o.en: Use at most N arguments per command line.

o.es: Ejecuta una vez por elemento y sustituye REEMPLAZO (p. ej. {}) por él.
o.en: Run once per item, replacing REPLACE (e.g. {}) with it.

o.es: Ejecuta hasta N procesos en paralelo.
o.en: Run up to N processes at a time.

o.es: No ejecuta el comando si la entrada está vacía.
o.en: Do not run the command if input is empty.

o.es: Muestra cada comando antes de ejecutarlo.
o.en: Print the command line before executing it.

o.es: Pregunta antes de ejecutar cada comando.
o.en: Prompt the user before running each command.

o.es: Usa DELIM como separador de elementos.
o.en: Input items are terminated by DELIM.

o.es: Lee los elementos de FILE en lugar de la entrada estándar.
o.en: Read items from FILE instead of standard input.
Set the end-of-file string to eof-str. If the end-of-file string occurs as a line of input, the rest of the input is ignored. If neither -E nor -e is used, no end-of-file string is used.

This option is a synonym for the -E option. Use -E instead, because it is POSIX compliant while this option is not. If eof-str is omitted, there is no end-of-file string. If neither -E nor -e is used, no end-of-file string is used.
This option is a synonym for -Ireplace-str if replace-str is specified. If the replace-str argument is missing, the effect is the same as -I{}. The -i option is deprecated; use -I instead.
Use at most max-lines nonblank input lines per command line. Trailing blanks cause an input line to be logically continued on the next input line. Implies -x.
Synonym for the -L option. Unlike -L, the max-lines argument is optional. If max-lines is not specified, it defaults to one. The -l option is deprecated since the POSIX standard specifies -L instead.
Reopen stdin as /dev/tty in the child process before executing the command. This is useful if you want xargs to run an interactive application.

Set the environment variable name to a unique value in each running child process. Values are reused once child processes exit. This can be used in a rudimentary load distribution scheme, for example.

Use at most max-chars characters per command line, including the command and initial-arguments and the terminating nulls at the ends of the argument strings. The largest allowed value is system-dependent, and is calculated as the argument length limit for exec, less the size of your environment, less 2048 bytes of headroom.

Display the limits on the command-line length which are imposed by the operating system, xargs' choice of buffer size and the -s option. Pipe the input from /dev/null (and perhaps specify --no-run-if-empty) if you don't want xargs to do anything.
Exit if the size (see the -s option) is exceeded.
Print a summary of the options to xargs and exit.
Print the version number of xargs and exit.
